title: Ordinary ringed exchange along an open immersion
statement: Let $g':X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] in a chosen Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let $r$ consist of coefficient sheaves of commutative rings at the four vertices, specified isomorphisms from their actual inverse-image rings along the four arrows, and coherence of the two composites [def-weil-pbc-strict-tower-operations; def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. If $g$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], the ordinary module counit mate $g^{-1}f_*\longrightarrow f'_*g'^{-1}$ of the canonical inverse-image square is an isomorphism. The ordinary adjunctions and square comparison are the normalized ones specified by these definitions; no derived categories, boundedness or finiteness hypotheses occur.

proof.text: For a weakly etale arrow h and any specified coefficient isomorphism, form the canonical object coprojection using the module adjunction unit and the unit of object-composition adjoint to base change. The latter adjunction induces an adjunction on ring sheaves. Compose its canonical ring comparison with the inverse of the specified coefficient isomorphism. The two ring identities follow from the sheaf adjunction unit and triangle identity. SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardAdj and uniqueness of left adjoints identify the module coprojection with a component of a natural isomorphism. It is therefore bijective, for all coefficients, including the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism; sites.tex Tag 00XZ, section-localize; sites-modules.tex Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules. Ordinary part of step 6 of lem-sf-ringed-restriction-exchange-open-descent.

proof.text: Apply unit_conjugateEquiv to exchangeModuleComposition. Its specified right-adjoint conjugate acts by the projection-preserving fibre-product pasting map, so its action on the composite unit is the pasted pair of units after this section restriction. Transport units across equality of coefficient-decorated morphisms by equality induction. Paste these identities for the two paths defining exchangeModuleSquare; coefficient coherence is exactly the required equality. This proves the sectionwise square unit equation without any open-immersion hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism; sites.tex Tag 00XZ, section-localize; sites-modules.tex Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules. Ordinary part of step 6 of lem-sf-ringed-restriction-exchange-open-descent.

proof.text: The chosen Cartesian identification and stability of open immersions under base change make the upper arrow open. For an object E over Y prime, form the canonical arrow from E times_{Y prime} X prime to E times_Y X, retaining its projection to X. Construct its inverse from two pullback lifts followed by sq.isoPullback.inv. The projection equations of the chosen square verify both inverse identities. Thus its restriction map on module sections is bijective.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism; sites.tex Tag 00XZ, section-localize; sites-modules.tex Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules. Ordinary part of step 6 of lem-sf-ringed-restriction-exchange-open-descent.

proof.text: Compute ordinary r on an adjunction unit section using the square unit equation, naturality and the right triangle identity. Apply naturality along the unit of object-composition adjoint to base change. The resulting site arrows agree by their fibre-product projections, so the mate sends each base coprojection of a section to the upper coprojection of its restriction along the canonical Cartesian arrow.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism; sites.tex Tag 00XZ, section-localize; sites-modules.tex Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules. Ordinary part of step 6 of lem-sf-ringed-restriction-exchange-open-descent.

proof.text: The two coprojections and the Cartesian restriction on sections are bijective. The section formula consequently makes every component of ordinary r bijective. The module-sheaf forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms, and objectwise isomorphisms of functors assemble to an isomorphism. There are no nonempty-open or nonzero-ring assumptions.
